MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  AUGUST 19, 2019

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 6:08 p.m. at Chandler Preserve, 95 Buckskin Ln, Rolling Hills Estates,
  California by CHAIR RETZ.

  1.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR RETZ led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Retz, Persichina, McCormick, Ciarolla & Bain

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Romanelli & Pope

  STAFF PRESENT:  Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager
  Michael Goldsmith, Maintenance Superintendent
  Cynthia Morquecho, Comm. Services Supervisor
  Daniel A-Haja, Comm. Services Coordinator

  3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF JULY 15, 2019

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF JULY 15,
  2019 AS AMENDED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None

  5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  None

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  STREET TREE REMOVAL REQUEST

  MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH provided a brief overview per the
  agenda material.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
AUGUST 19, 2019
   COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA suggested that if trees follow the criteria for being
  removed, not all tree removals need to be brought to the Commission. He noted that in
  the past, Commissioners were given a packet with addresses of trees meeting the removal
  criteria and would assess whether or not the tree should go.

  CHAIR RETZ recommends that the criteria for tree removal be reviewed by the
  Commission and staff further streamline the process of tree removal.

  MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH noted that the proposed tree to be
  removed on Dunwood Road needed to be removed and could not be trimmed back to
  prevent damage to the sidewalk.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  CIAROLLA to:

  APPROVE THE REMOVAL AND REPLACEMENT OF ONE BRAZILIAN
  PEPPER TREE LOCATED AT 26331 DUNWOOD ROAD AT THE COST
  OF THE APPLICANT.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  B.  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT

  COMMUNITY SERVICES COORDINATOR AHAJA provided an overview per agenda
  material.

  CHAIR RETZ recommends that a reciprocal agreement be in place for the cancellation
  clause. He also disagrees with the Confidentiality Agreement, since what the City
  discusses is often public record and further expressed concerns related to the cancellation
  policy and fees within Exhibit B.

  COMMUNITY SERVICES COORDINATOR AHAJA recommends that the agreement be
  approved upon edits agreed upon between Parade Management and City Attorney.
  CHAIR RETZ tabled for the next regular Park and Activities Commission meeting.

  C.  TABER GROVE PHASE I AND II UPDATE

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO provided an overview per
  agenda material.

  CHAIR RETZ wanted next steps clarified that Phases I and II of the project are
  independent of each other and the encroachment by the neighbor is also separate from
  the project.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS stated the next step would be to clarify the stages
  of the project and that encroachment fees would be charged to the affected property owner
  after the project is completed.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
AUGUST 19, 2019
   CHAIR RETZ asked the cost of Phase I implementation of the project. COMMUNITY
  SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO responded that the City has not yet received
  an engineer’s estimate but are expecting it soon.

  CHAIR RETZ stated that the homeowner that has the noted encroachments previously
  indicated that the homeowners’ association was against both Phase I and Phase II of the
  project and asked if this had been confirmed, but Phase I should proceed as is having
  received neighborhood buy-in.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK questioned if there was any dispute over Phase I.
  CHAIR RETZ responded the homeowner did dispute both phases.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS noted that previous records reflect that the
  neighborhood and homeowner agreed with Phase I and the City proceeded as such with
  commitment from the Palos Verdes Land Conservancy for the donation and a contract
  with Willdan Engineering. She additionally explained that the opposition arose when
  Phase II was proposed.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if staff has heard from the neighborhood regarding
  the project. Staff confirmed they had not received any further input from the neighborhood.

  CHAIR RETZ noted another concern he heard was that the proposed additional trees
  planted may impact the view of traffic around the corner.

  MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH noted that the additional trees will be
  in the grove portion and would not get tall enough or be in the way to obstruct street view.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted the concern also raised by the resident that Phase II could
  be a nuisance because children would kick balls, run in the street, and climb on the
  retaining walls. While she expressed she does not agree with this perspective, she asks
  that before the decision of Phase II be completed, staff considered what safety measures
  should be considered as part of Phase I to reduce the potential of a nuisance.

  CHAIR RETZ suggested a three-fence be considered around top of the ridge near Phase
  I that goes perpendicular to Palos Verdes Drive East.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS noted that staff can assess the area to for additional
  fencing as part of Phase I.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked about the history of efforts in contacting the local HOA.
  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO stated that conversations were
  held with the neighborhood but no formal letter has been found in the file. ASSISTANT
  CITY MANAGER stated a letter was sent but not seen in the file and staff will continue
  looking through the record for further details.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK stated that there is fencing along the road in the area.
  He additionally stated that concerns about balls bouncing out of bounds is a scenario that
  could happen at all parks.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
AUGUST 19, 2019
   COMMISSIONER BAIN noted that the objection has been raised so we should consider
  solutions.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked what the timeline was to respond to the HOA.
  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO responded that staff plans to
  develop a community meeting to receive feedback. ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER stated
  the meeting would be held after the City Celebration.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked once trees are cleared from Phase I, is there a current
  barren space where the three trees are proposed. MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT
  GOLDSMITH affirmed. COMMISSIONER BAIN stated that one of the concerns was that
  more people would hang out in the area and the trees could possibly create cover.
  MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH noted that the sycamore trees used,
  have low amounts of undergrowth and does not make a great encampment area for
  people gathering. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK added that there are many other park
  pocket areas more attractive for gathering than this particular area.

  CHAIR RETZ received and filed the report.

  7.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  COMMISSIONER BAIN commended the maintenance crew due to the improvements to
  Highridge Park. COMMISSIONER BAIN noted some puddles by the trails near the homes
  and stated that the men’s restroom needed more thorough cleaning. She stated that the
  park is a lot nicer and children’s area is safe. She stated that fence posts should be
  considered to be replaced in the future due to termite damage.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if the shed at Ernie Howlett Park had been
  removed. COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO affirmed the shed
  had been removed.

  CHAIR RETZ noted fence posts were down on Palos Verdes Drive North just past the golf
  course, just past the 30 MPH sign and nearby the church. He will share the photos with
  staff.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted he has pictures for areas at George F Canyon
  where some trees are hanging with low branches, with one dead limb hanging along the
  trail. He stated that the water fountain is getting mossy and not draining anymore. He
  asked if a scenic point could be created where the Girl Scouts have a wooden entrance
  sign area with a picnic table or seating. He noted the sign is in need of repair.
  MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH responded that area is a turn out and
  the City has had a bench there before. ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS stated it
  could be a possible Eagle Scout project. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK explained that
  during a steep part of the trail, there was an area where there should be fencing

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
AUGUST 19, 2019
   considered. He also stated there were three mountain bikers on the trail even though there
  is enough signage prohibiting bikes along the trail.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted that a fence near Fern Creek Trail was collapsed and
  broken, behind 11 Ponderosa.

  COMMISSIONER ROMENALLI by verbal report from COMMUNITY SERVICES
  SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO suggested posting community reminder in the next
  newsletter that alcohol is not permitted at Rockbluff Park.

  B.  CITY CELEBRATION SUBCOMMITTEE UPDATE VERBAL REPORT

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA noted that there were some time changes in the schedule
  and volunteers are needed for the Poker Ride and Pepper Tree booth.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted that this is the first time we needed Poker Ride
  volunteers.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA stated that Melody Colbert is no longer organizing the
  Poker Ride prizes and none have been received by the City at this time.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN reported that she met a resident who has a band that should be
  considered for entertainment at the City Celebration.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  REMOVAL OF JUNIPER TREES IN MEDIAN ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH (VERBAL REPORT)

  MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT GOLDMSITH reported 18 Juniper Trees on
  Dapplegray Lane need to be taken out due to fire hazard. COMMISSIONER BAIN asked
  if there was a plan to replace the Juniper trees scheduled for removal. MAINTENANCE
  SUPERINTENDENT GOLDMSITH indicated there is no plan at this time but the City had
  been working on a Master Median Landscape Plan in the future which would consider this
  area.

  B.  SILVER SPUR LITTLE LEAGUE SHED UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted that Silver Spur Little
  League withdrew their request for the shed to be placed and removed it in August. She
  noted that an additional meeting would be scheduled with the Little League, Youth Sports
  Subcommittee and staff.

  COMMISSIONERS BAIN and CIAROLLA stated the Little League was very apologetic
  and reported that this happened in transition of their new leaders as reported to the City
  Council. COMMISSIONER BAIN stated she learned from the representatives at the City
  Council meeting that the League is not attracting older athletes as easy and they are
  seeking to modify the organization to be better attractive. COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA
  reported that based on his experience, sports participation everywhere is declining.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
AUGUST 19, 2019
   She further detailed that the Little League explained the shed that was placed was to be
  competitive with other fields with score keeping and announcing. COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA responded that a score board is kept but may be broken and repair is their
  responsibility per the contract.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN also reported that Little League representatives ask that the water
  fountain be placed at a different location than where the scorekeepers shed was placed.
  MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH responded that the water fountain
  placement is flexible.

  C.  “BUTCHER PARK” UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted that Metropolitan Water
  District will start their Reservoir project in September 2020 with a projected end in August
  2021. Staff noted that $150,000 was requested for parks development and pavement on
  Palos Verdes Drive North and East.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted that $200,000 was initially offered for parks
  development and pavement and asked that the City clarify the amount. COMMISSIONER
  BAIN asked that we confirm the timeline on the project.

  SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted that staff will clarify timeline and amount offered for
  parks development.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL MEETING ACTIONS OF JULY 23, 2019

  Received and filed.

  B.  CITY COUNCIL MEETING ACTIONS OF AUGUST 13, 2019

  Received and filed.

  C.  PLANNING COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF AUGUST 5, 2019

  Received and filed.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  VETERANS MEMORIAL

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted that she is working with a
  person interested in donating $5,000 toward a memorial that would honor all who have
  served in any branch of the military in any capacity. She also reported that the donor
  would like for the City to host a dedication ceremony for the memorial once established.
  The item will return at the next Commission meeting with a proposal.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
AUGUST 19, 2019
   B.  MUNICIPAL CODE UPDATE – SPECIAL EVENTS

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO is reviewing special event fees,
  sponsorship levels, and permitting process and plan to develop the areas further and will
  return to the Commission for input.

  11.  PARK TOURS

  The Park and Activities Commission toured Chandler Preserve and noted the following:
  • Local plants fauna have been coming back to the land.
  • Volunteers are a large part of maintaining the land.
  • PV Blue Butterflies are found in this preserve and efforts are being made to bring
  them back to the area.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA to,

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 7:34 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES MEETING ON SEPTEMBER 16, 2019 AT 7:00 P.M., WHICH WILL
  MEET AT CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS, 4045 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  _____________________________
  Daniel A-Haja  Cynthia Morquecho
  Community Services Coordinator  Community Services Supervisor

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
AUGUST 19, 2019
